messages:
sara: heads up — eval-runner CI failing on BERTScore for quant int8 bring-up. on model x-qat-int8 we see ~0.07 drop vs float32 on dev subset. logs attached.
ci-bot: TEST FAILED: eval-runner/bertscore_regression (build: 4562) — https://ci.redwood/4562/artifacts (bscore-diff.txt) :warning:
sara: copying minimal repro below — running bert_score.score on preds vs refs, same prompts, different scores. code:```python
from bert_score import score
hyp = open('preds.txt').read().splitlines()
ref = open('refs.txt').read().splitlines()
P, R, F = score(hyp, ref, lang='en', rescale_with_baseline=False, batch_size=64)
print(F.mean().item())
```
kai: assigning to me. can you paste the failing per-example diffs? is this BERTScore impl or tokenization mismatch?
sara: artifact snippet: `id, bscore_float, bscore_int8, delta` — many deltas negative, concentrated on long responses. attaching small excerpt: `1234,0.87,0.78,-0.09; 1256,0.82,0.79,-0.03; 1299,0.90,0.82,-0.08`
amar: two quick checks: 1) tokenizers/version diffs (hf-tokenizers can change normalization) 2) quantization noise on embedding kernels. also verify we’re using same BERTScore baseline/rescaling flags for both runs.
lia: CI artifact /artifacts/4562/bscore-diff.txt shows distribution — median delta ~ -0.02 but long tail to -0.12. long examples worse.
kai: suspect ordering bug in the runner: if refs/preds get misaligned you get large deltas. can you grep for places we convert sets/maps to list without deterministic sort?
sara: ugh — found it: in passk dedupe we do `unique_ids = set(ids)` then later `for idx, out in enumerate(outputs): pair = (list(unique_ids)[idx], out)` — that reorders.
marta: :eyes: that would definitely explain spikes. ordering bug + quant noise amplifies apparent regression.
eval-bot: queued CI run with ordering fix PR #4567 — running float32 + int8 comparisons now.
kai: additional recommended fixes: canonicalize text before metric (NFKC normalize, collapse whitespace, strip trailing newlines), pin hf-tokenizers version in CI, and add deterministic seed where applicable.
amar: also add embedding-norm check in runner — assert L2 norm distribution not wildly different between float32 and quantized runs, to help triage.
lia: I'll add a runbook note about BERTScore sensitivity to tiny embedding shifts and put pointers to when to prefer ROUGE/ExactMatch for discrete tasks.
ci-bot: build #4567 queued. status: running tests on float32... then int8.
eval-bot: small follow-up — please add a unit test that loads a fixed small set (10 examples) and asserts pairing is stable across runner invocations (repeat 5 times).
sara: thanks. tldr: root cause is nondeterministic pairing in runner + tokenization bump. mitigations: deterministic ordering, canonicalize text, pin tokenizer version, add regression tests for bscore deltas and pairing stability. assigning @kai to PR for canonicalization + tests, @amar to add embedding-norm check. will monitor next CI. :thumbsup:
